IMPLEMENT STORY #433, SLICE 1: Bound driver frames, diagnostics, checkpoint buffering and local UI connections

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-433-slice-1, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (on a branch from before #423, PR #544, the old form is --test suppressions), and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (since #423, each crate's integration tests are one binary, run as --test it FILE::, and a new tests/*.rs is registered as mod FILE; in its crate's tests/it.rs, which layering::test_targets enforces; on a branch from before #423 the old --test FILE forms stand)
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending: this seat is non-interactive, so ending the turn ends the process and your result file is never written.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#433)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- The implement phase alone changes files and commits. Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY whatever this text asks elsewhere: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit; it reports each finding, and a returned finding is fixed by the implementer in a later round.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is origin/main as you find it (90d94dd8 or later). Main lands only through the merge queue. Relevant since the issue was filed: #403 (a timed-out attempt ends its whole process tree; bounded teardown, which this story reuses), #394 (the contention hold's HELD_BYTES bound in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/checkpoints.rs; see the operator's 2026-09-28 comment on #433), #415 (scratch lifecycle), #353 slice 1 (typed errors in brokkr-core: a new refusal is a typed variant with exact Display text).
- Operator ruling, 2026-09-26, the threat model for every gate: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual. Here that means: a runaway or buggy driver (a megabyte line with no newline, a stderr flood, a checkpoint loop) must not exhaust the engine's memory, and the run must end in a typed, truthful outcome.
- Host tool versions, as ci.yml pins them: typos 1.50.2, shellcheck 0.11.0, zizmor 1.30.1, actionlint 1.7.12, lychee (setup-lychee's digest), jscpd 5.3.2, cargo-shear 1.14.0, cargo-crap 0.5.0, cargo-public-api 0.52.0, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, stable Rust 1.98.0 (rust-toolchain.toml), MSRV 1.88.0.
- On this host typos, shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and lychee live in ~/.local/bin, and jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin.
- Tests that spawn processes: since #403 the test binary is a subreaper engine with one attempt registry. A test that deliberately leaves a process alive must run that launch in a child process of the test binary, as process/tests.rs's `role` pattern does, or a parallel test will read the leftover as a stray. Fake drivers for floods are small scripts or the existing test driver fixtures; no provider is contacted.
- Other work runs in parallel on other branches. Stay out of these files unless your story needs them, and say so in notes if it does:
  - #429 slice 2 (brokkr-core policy.rs and policy/audit.rs, bundle.rs's compile, shipped policy.json tables, witness pins);
  - #345 slice 1 (brokkr-core envelope.rs and fold.rs, engine.rs's GATE-MOVED-HEAD sites, brokkr-view): landing;
  - Decision 0065 slice two (another session): do NOT touch cli_args.rs, broker.rs, broker/*, secret*, observer.rs, agents/mcp.rs or bundle/mcp.rs.
- THIS STORY IS #433, SLICE 1, on branch story-433-slice-1, cut from main and checked out here. The issue was measured at 8d7da844: re-measure each site.
- SLICE 1 IS THE DRIVER TRANSPORT ONLY: crates/brokkr-protocol/src/process.rs and what it returns. Today (re-measure): forward() reads each stdout protocol line with an unbounded read_line into a String; read_stderr() drains the driver's stderr whole with read_to_end; run_attempt_resuming() retains every checkpoint in a Vec<Value> until finish().
  1. Limits: a frame byte limit (a protocol line, checked BEFORE the line is allocated whole or parsed as JSON, so a stream with no newline and invalid UTF-8 are both refused bounded), a stderr retention limit (keep a bounded head and tail with the count of bytes dropped, so the diagnostic stays useful and the pipe is still drained so the driver never blocks on a full pipe), a result byte limit if the result frame is not already covered by the frame limit, and a checkpoint retention limit (count and pending bytes). Defaults are named constants with units in their names or docs, held in one place; zero or an overflowing value can never mean unlimited. Configuration ownership (realms, adapter or recipe) is a ruling: take constants now, injectable through the transport's constructor so tests use small limits, and name the configuration question in notes for the PR's Ruling line.
  2. Typed outcomes: an exceeded frame, result or checkpoint limit ends the attempt with a typed resource-limit failure that names the limit, its unit and a bounded, redacted piece of evidence (never the whole rejected input). Effects may already have happened when a driver floods, so the attempt is not reported succeeded nor safely retryable: reuse the existing lifecycle-uncertainty outcome (indeterminate) the way #394's held-bytes overflow does, and reuse #403's bounded teardown to end the driver's tree. A stderr flood alone is not a failure: it truncates the retained diagnostic and says so.
  3. Tests, provider-free, each with a small injected limit and an exact assertion on the outcome and its text: an oversized frame, a no-newline frame, invalid UTF-8 in a frame, a stderr flood (the driver still finishes and the retained stderr is head + marker + tail with the exact dropped count), an oversized result, and a checkpoint flood. Each beside its control under the limit. Each bound by a compiling mutation that removes the bound.
  4. Compatibility: normal drivers, the journal bytes within the existing contracts and the driver conformance tests keep passing unchanged. No contract, fixture, policy or reference file changes.
- NOT THIS SLICE: the loopback UI's request, header, connection and SSE limits (crates/brokkr-cli/src/ui.rs: slice 2), spill files and their cleanup (slice 3), #342's measurements. Name them in notes as follow-ups.
- Gates as usual: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol, -p brokkr-runtime and -p brokkr-cli (crate-scoped), clippy -D warnings, fmt, typos --hidden, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. Integration tests run as --test it FILE::. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's. Name the public-API changes in notes.

FIX ROUND 433b. The first round committed 8c0fc603 on this branch: the driver's stdout lines, its kept stderr and its report's checkpoints are bounded, and a driver past a limit ends indeterminate. Its review returned a SECURITY-HOLD; the chief's text is below, verbatim. This round adds ONE commit on top of 8c0fc603 that fixes the returned findings. Do not rewrite or squash 8c0fc603.
- FIX (1) HIGH, security, exactly as the chief asks. Evidence for a refused frame carries NO content of the refused input: a byte count, the class of the first byte, and a digest (for example the first 16 hex characters of its SHA-256) are enough to correlate it without disclosing it. Apply the same rule to the pre-existing unreadable-driver-message site (process.rs about :337, "unreadable driver message: {e}: {line}"), which journals the whole non-JSON line: the outcome names the parse error's kind and position and the line's length and digest, never its text. If a conformance or engine test pins that site's text, move the pin to the new bytes and say so in notes (new runs only; no existing journal or fixture changes). Bind non-disclosure with exact tests: plant a synthetic credential-shaped token (an obviously fake value such as "sk-test-NOTASECRET-0000") at the head of an oversized line, in a non-JSON line, and in a line that is both, and assert the exact outcome text and that the token appears nowhere in it or in the journaled payload. Record a compiling removal control for each: restoring the raw head must fail the test. The tests that asserted the quoted head is present (limits/tests.rs about :150, :165, :187, :208) move to the content-free form.
- FIX (2) MEDIUM: add a SHORT proposed decision for the new semantics, under docs/decisions/, numbered with the next free number in docs/decisions/README.md at your base, Status: proposed. It records: the four default limits and their units; that a driver past a frame, result or checkpoint limit ends its attempt indeterminate (lifecycle uncertainty, never succeeded or safely retryable) through #403's teardown; that stderr past its limit keeps head and tail with the dropped count and is no failure; that refusal evidence is content-free; and that configuration ownership of the limits is left open for a later ruling. Add its row to docs/decisions/README.md as the existing proposed rows are written. Only the operator accepts it; do not mark it accepted.
- FIX (3) LOW: Exceeded::Checkpoints names its evidence as counts (checkpoints held and bytes held), never as line content, with an exact text test.
- Carried, do not act: the arrivals channel budget (INFO, slice 3 or #464) and the endless-line test under the M1 mutation (state in notes whether you ran it now).
- Never resolve a finding by weakening a refusal or a test. If a finding is wrong on your read, prove it with a command and its output, and say so in notes.
- Gates, all clean: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol, -p brokkr-runtime and -p brokkr-cli (crate-scoped), clippy -D warnings, fmt, typos --hidden, quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's.

THE REVIEW, VERBATIM:

REVIEW CHIEF, story #433 slice 1, commit 8c0fc603 over 90d94dd8. Panel: three positions joined (adversarial=security-hold, correctness=residual, glm=residual), all in vocabulary, no __member-schema-invalid__. No member text addressed this gate or argued for a verdict from it; glm's 'none returns to implement' is its own verdict and is outranked by the floor. The panel reported security-hold, so this seat rules security-hold; the floor is unconditional and the finding is confirmed on my own read. Read-only: no tracked file changed, no commit; git status clean. SURVIVING FINDINGS, deduplicated. (1) HIGH, security, raised by adversarial and independently by correctness (its MEDIUM #2 is the same defect): rejected-frame evidence is bounded but not redacted. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/process/limits.rs:149-153 evidence() copies the first 64 bytes of the refused line ASCII-escaped; Exceeded::Frame (line 74) prints them as 'it began ...'; outcome() (lines 92-96) puts that text into AttemptOutcome::Indeterminate.reason; crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs:1962-1969 appends that reason unchanged into the EffectIndeterminate payload, which is append-only and hash-chained. The adversarial member's provider-free probe showed a synthetic credential at the head of an oversized line reproduced verbatim in the outcome. Slice 1 item 2 asks for bounded, REDACTED evidence; decision 0012's context says a secret journaled once is permanent. No test binds non-disclosure: the new tests assert the quoted head is present (limits/tests.rs:150, 165, 187, 208), the opposite of redaction. Same family, pre-existing and named by glm as INFO: process.rs:337 'unreadable driver message: {e}: {line}' still journals the whole non-JSON line, now capped at 16 MiB by the frame limit; it is a wider exposure than the new path, so a fix that redacts only the new site leaves the slice's redaction claim hollow. Return to implement: replace raw head content with content-free evidence (byte count, first byte class, or a digest), apply the same rule to the unreadable-message site or name in notes why not, and add an exact non-disclosure test with a removal control (0071 ruling 9). Under the 2026-09-26 threat-model ruling this is accidental-misuse territory and the house table reserves high for a weakened refusal or hidden fail-open path; I carry the panel's HIGH because the floor forbids lowering, and the operator may rule the severity when accepting the fix. (2) MEDIUM, correctness: no proposed decision document accompanies the new semantics (four default limits, a new indeterminate ending for a driver past them, head+tail stderr retention). grep of docs/decisions finds none for the transport bounds; the house rule and docs/decisions/README.md line 1-5 require one for a semantic change. Carried as reported. Context for the operator: the task framing routes operator choices to the PR's Ruling: line, and #353 slice 1 (90d94dd8) landed without a decision document, so the operator may rule the Ruling: line satisfies it; that ruling is not mine to make. (3) LOW, glm, 0071 ruling 8 and acceptance 'every exceeded limit reports its limit/unit and bounded evidence': limits.rs:76-77 Exceeded::Checkpoints names limit and unit but no evidence, unlike Frame and CheckpointBytes. Confirmed. Fix with counts (checkpoints held, bytes held), never with raw line content, so the fix to (1) is not undone here. INFO, glm, follow-ups outside this slice: the arrivals channel between transport and sink is count-bounded (ARRIVALS=64) with each item now at most 16 MiB, so the attempt-wide budget across hold, channel and report stays untyped for slice 3/#464; the endless-line test was not run under the M1 mutation (the commit says so). MY OWN READ, no new finding: read_frame refuses at the first byte past the limit via fill_buf before UTF-8 decode or JSON parse, and the underflow guard holds because line.len() <= limit at every loop top; retained_stderr keeps head+tail and counts dropped bytes while draining to EOF; Retained::keep refuses before on_checkpoint so a refused checkpoint is neither journaled nor kept; end() routes Exceeded through finish() and tree::end, which is #403's teardown; Stdout/Ended/Frame/Exceeded are exhaustive enums (ruling 2); Exceeded is thiserror (ruling 8); run_attempt_resuming shed its too_many_lines expect and suppressions.txt and too-many-lines.txt were regenerated to match. Frozen surfaces untouched in the six-file diff. OBSERVED BY THIS SEAT: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked process::limits:: printed 7 passed; git status --short printed nothing. Other gates were observed by the panel members and are theirs, not re-run here; exact coverage and remote CI are pending with the controller. Follow-ups the implementer already named: UI limits (slice 2), spill files and cleanup (slice 3), #342 measurements, configuration ownership of the limits (realms, adapter or recipe) for the PR's Ruling: line.

THE ISSUE (#433), verbatim:

Part of #330. Architecture review against `main` at `8d7da844` (2026-09-26). Related: #342 (measurement budgets), #403 (process lifetime), #394 (checkpoint contention), #415 (scratch lifecycle).

**Evidence and impact**

[Driver transport](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/blob/8d7da8443726ec86b0385c1a3d3816c8a01aa954/crates/brokkr-protocol/src/process.rs#L134) drains stderr into an unrestricted `String`, reads protocol lines without a byte limit, and retains checkpoints in a `Vec`. [The loopback UI](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/blob/8d7da8443726ec86b0385c1a3d3816c8a01aa954/crates/brokkr-cli/src/ui.rs#L1144) reads request lines/headers without explicit size or read-time limits and starts one thread per connection. The UI's loopback binding limits exposure; this report does not claim a remote exploit. No exhaustion attack was run.

#342 measures CPU/heap/binary/prompt budgets; it does not implement runtime protocol admission limits. #394 proposes buffering through a held database lock; that buffer needs a bound and a truthful failure path. This issue owns those runtime constraints.

**Work**

1. Define explicit frame, result and diagnostic byte limits; checkpoint count/rate and pending-byte limits; spill-file byte limits where used; and UI request/header/connection/read/write limits. Specify defaults, units and configuration ownership. Values must not overflow or become unlimited through zero/negative conversion.
2. Enforce frame limits before unbounded allocation/JSON parsing, including a stream with no newline and invalid UTF-8. Preserve bounded redacted diagnostic context for a refusal rather than storing the full rejected input in an error.
3. Stream/spool diagnostics and checkpoints with bounded memory, bounded disk use and clear retention. Preserve required evidence and ordering; no silent loss of terminal events or duplicate checkpoint replay. Coordinate lock recovery with #394 and cleanup with #415.
4. Reject excess UI work before spawning unlimited handlers. Bound slow request/response clients and release capacity when connections disappear. Preserve long-lived SSE behavior within declared limits.
5. Journal/return typed resource-limit failures. If effects may already have occurred, use lifecycle uncertainty rules rather than reporting an unearned successful or safely retryable outcome. Reuse #403's bounded teardown.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Provider-free tests exercise an oversized/no-newline frame, stderr flood, oversized result, checkpoint flood and lock-held buffer growth with a small injected limit.
- [ ] Peak retained memory and spill size remain within declared budgets; #342 measures representative production-size fixtures.
- [ ] Every exceeded limit reports its limit/unit and bounded evidence, and terminates or parks within the declared cleanup bound.
- [ ] Slow/oversized HTTP requests and excess connections do not consume unbounded memory or threads; disconnected SSE clients release resources.
- [ ] Spill files are safely cleaned after terminal ownership is established, including restart after a killed owner.
- [ ] Normal drivers, journal bytes within the existing contract and UI behavior retain their compatibility tests.

Keep process cleanup owned by #403 and performance regression measurements owned by #342. Runtime limits must be implemented, not inferred from a benchmark passing.


THE OPERATOR RULING ON #433 (2026-09-28), verbatim:

**The spill from #394, ruled to land here (operator, 2026-09-28).**

#394's contention hold is bounded by `HELD_BYTES`: 16 MiB plus one row of any size, declared at `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/checkpoints.rs` around lines 34-38 at `39b7e5f0`. There is no spill file. A burst past a full hold settles the attempt indeterminate and says how many rows were lost.

Two more buffers that predate #394 are still unbounded:
- the panel's mpsc channel (`engine.rs`, around line 2007);
- `AttemptReport.checkpoints` in brokkr-protocol.

This issue owns the spill file and the attempt-wide bound across all three. The other #394 follow-ups (timer, batching, counted drops) are in #464.

exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the

change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
